compareCandidate.label: Skin vs. bark
compareCandidate.description: A tree's bark and our skin both protect, but skin is alive throughout, senses touch, sweats to cool us, and constantly repairs itself - bark is a nonliving protective layer.

plainLanguageExplanation: The skin is the body's largest organ - in an adult it covers about 2 square meters. It has two main layers. The outer epidermis is the thin protective surface; its outer cells wear away and are constantly replaced. Below it, the thicker dermis contains blood vessels, nerves that sense touch, sweat glands, oil glands, and hair roots. The skin has many jobs: it protects the body from damage, germs, and water loss; it helps control temperature through sweating and blood flow; it lets you feel touch, pressure, heat, and cold; and it repairs itself when cut. A deeper layer, the hypodermis, attaches it to the body.

whyItMatters: The skin is your body's first line of defense and its largest sense organ. Understanding it explains why you sweat, why cuts heal, why you can feel a light touch, and why your skin constantly replaces itself.
didYouKnow: You shed about 30,000 to 40,000 dead skin cells every minute - your skin completely renews its outer layer roughly every month.
